cost.description:
Direct costs are 15,68€/hour (more information on fees is available in 'BIGAN>Services>Fees' https://bigan.iacs.es/en/services/fees) and include data
request processing, a) data mining, ETL processing, and c) security and quality assurance.
The service includes defining queries and extracting information on available information sources, extracting the requested data and completing the ETL processes for complying with the requested common data model specification. The global cost of a typical data request for a population-level research question
is usually under 2000 euros and is served in approximately under 3 weeks time.

data_quality_assurance: Set up of scientific and technical committee
Use of tools for automatic checks
Consistency verified with data models and standards

We have implemented comprehensive documented procedures for quality assurance in our project "Healthcare Pathways of Heart Failure Patients within the Spanish National Health System and its Impact on Health Outcomes (CONCEPT-HF)." These procedures are designed to ensure the highest standards of data quality and reliability.
First, we have established a scientific and technical committee responsible for overseeing all aspects of data quality. This committee includes experts in data science, clinical research, and information technology, who provide guidance and oversight throughout the data collection and processing stages.
Second, we use advanced tools for automatic checks to identify and correct errors in the data. These tools perform validation checks to ensure that the data conforms to the specified format and meets predefined quality criteria. For instance, they check for missing values, outliers, and inconsistencies.
Third, our data is meticulously verified to conform to format specifications and consistency is checked against established data models and standards. This includes using standardized vocabularies like CDISC for clinical data and HL7 FHIR for healthcare data, ensuring interoperability and consistency.
Additionally, we conduct regular data audits and reviews to identify and rectify any discrepancies. All data processing steps are thoroughly documented, and version control systems are used to track changes, ensuring transparency and accountability.
By implementing these rigorous quality assurance procedures, we ensure that our data is accurate, reliable, and suitable for high-quality research and analysis.
dataset.description:
The CONCEPT-HF public health cohort links selected variables from primary care or hospital admission for Heart Failure (HF), covering a global population of approximately 19 million inhabitants for three regions of Spain (Andalucía, Aragón, País Vasco). This cohort includes all patients admitted to hospital due to HF in public hospitals and complementary information on patient attributes (i.e., comorbidities, healthcare system contacts, prescribed HF drugs) and patient health outcomes (i.e., readmissions and mortality). Original data is maintained and updated daily by the different health systems of each region described. A common data model specification with the required information to achieve the expected results of the research question is provided as supporting documentation
at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.11234699 - Common Data Model Specification. Data is provided pseudonymised  and granted by the Andalusian Ethical Research Committee.

format:
Comma Separated Values.
The original data is processed by Research Service of the General Secretariat of Public Health in R&D&I in Health of the Regional Government of Andalusia, the Directorate of Healthcare Services of Osakidetza - Basque Health Service and BIGAN under the privacy and security policies of the Health Sciences Institute in Aragon and in compliance with the specifications provided by the common data model within the data access request and provided as a pipe-separated CSV file using UTF-8 format.

host.description:
Zenodo provides a rich interface which enables linking research outputs to datasets and funding information. Some of its advantages are:
1. Citeable and discoverable: All uploads get a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) to make them easily and uniquely citeable. All open content is harvestable via OAI-PMH by third parties.
2. Supports versioning: Via a top-level DOI, it can support all the different versions of a file.
3. Trusted, reliable, safe: Data is stored at CERN, which has considerable knowledge and experience operating large scale digital repositories. Data files and metadata are kept in multiple online and offline copies.
4. Includes funding information and makes reporting easier: Zenodo allows to link uploads to grants from more than 11 funders such as European Commission, National Science Foundation and Wellcome Trust. Zenodo is further integrated into reporting lines for research funded by the European Commission via OpenAIRE. 
5. Includes article level metrics: Tracks attention for scholarship uploaded.
6. Flexible licensing: Zenodo encourages to share research as openly as possible to maximize use and re-use the research results. 
7. Reviewing: Research materials can set to share with reviewers only, and also embargoed.
8. Software preservation made simple: Zenodo is integrated with GitHub.
9. Supports FAIR principles: Zenodo makes data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable.

distribution.available_until:
The dataset/output from the project will be made accessible as follows:
Open Access Data:
Immediate Release: All data designated for open access will be made accessible immediately upon the conclusion of the project. This ensures timely dissemination of research findings and maximizes the impact and utility of the data for the research community and other stakeholders.
Restricted Access Data:
Delayed Release: Data requiring restricted access due to sensitivity, confidentiality, or legal considerations will be made accessible 12 months after the project has ended. This delay allows sufficient time for the implementation of necessary data protection measures and for the completion of any additional analysis or publications by the project team.
Embargo Periods:
Conditional Release: In certain cases, specific datasets may be subject to an embargo period extending beyond 12 months. Such cases will be clearly justified based on contractual obligations, intellectual property considerations, or other legitimate interests as stipulated in the Grant Agreement. The duration of the embargo will be determined on a case-by-case basis, ensuring a balance between data protection and accessibility.
Final Accessibility Date:
Maximum Accessibility: All project data, including those under embargoed access, will be made fully accessible no later than 24 months after the project has ended. This ensures that all data generated by the project will eventually be available to the wider research community, supporting ongoing and future research efforts. The only exception will be the restricted access data. 
By adhering to this timeline, the CONCEPT-HF project ensures that the data is made accessible in a manner that respects legal, ethical, and contractual requirements while promoting transparency and reuse of research data.

dataset.preservation_statement: Andalucía, Aragon and the Basque Country has a regional mandate to curate and maintain original data requests (and related ETL queries) in the long term and report on the re-use of health data for research purposes.

security_and_privacy.description:
Original data is de-identified and pseudonymised using a Hash function before being extracted and then served for research purposes encrypted and compressed, requiring a secure password to decompress the files.
The data request process includes a feasibility and security assessment of the information requirements specified in the data model considering data minimization to achieve the research objectives.

dataset.title: Description of the Data Management Plan (DMP) for the Healthcare Pathways of Heart Failure Patients within the Spanish National Health System and its Impact on Health Outcomes (CONCEPT-HF) Project.

dmp.description:
This publication corresponds to the Data Management Plan (DMP) for "Care pathways of heart failure patients within the Spanish National Health System and its impact on health outcomes (CONCEPT-HF)" project.
The CONCEPT-HF project will introduce a novel concept, the healthcare trajectory, as an analytical tool for examining patient management in HF with the objective of identifying deviations that impact health outcomes and thus enabling the establishment of corrective measures. Given the substantial amount and variety of data to be analyzed, the use of process mining techniques will be indispensable to ensure the precision, consistency, and homogeneity necessary for robust and high-quality analysis.
A brief structured description of the research question, the proposed study design, and the cohort definition is provided below.

project.description:
The Carlos III Health Institute (ISCIII) is a public biomedical research institution in Spain, under the Ministry of Science and Innovation. Its main mission is to promote the generation of scientific knowledge in the field of health and encourage its application to improve the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases. Among its activities, the ISCIII manages and funds research projects to drive innovation and scientific advancement.

A competitively funded project is one that has obtained funds through a rigorous and competitive evaluation process. In this process, projects are assessed and selected based on their scientific quality, feasibility, relevance, and potential impact in the field of study. Projects selected for competitive funding must demonstrate excellence and the ability to significantly contribute to the advancement of knowledge and the improvement of public health.
